42967961.titulo: Key factors for growth and phosphate uptake by Acinetobacter tjernbergiae.
42967961.autores: Brück J, Täuber S, Ackermann L, Schittkowski H, Neubauer P, Junne S

resumo_blocos.racional: A recuperação de fósforo a partir de efluentes é um imperativo tecnológico devido à escassez de reservas minerais, mas cepas de Acinetobacter frequentemente exibem limitação estequiométrica de biomassa, impedindo taxas industriais viáveis de captura de fosfato. A literatura debatia se o gargalo limitante residia na cinética enzimática intrínseca das polifosfato quinases ou em carências coadjuvantes de cofatores metálicos fundamentais para o metabolismo respiratório bacteriano. Diante desse paradoxo, os autores hipotetizaram que o ajuste racional da concentração de ferro solúvel aliviaria restrições energéticas e respiratórias, viabilizando uma densidade celular ótima capaz de sustentar taxas recordes de captação dependentes de carbono e disparar o fenótipo de hiperacumulação ('overplus').
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O estudo utilizou a cepa bacteriana Acinetobacter tjernbergiae cultivada comparativamente em frascos agitados (shake flasks) e em biorreatores de escala laboratorial com controle fino de aeração, pH e taxa de agitação. Foram implementadas curvas de titulação de micronutrientes, destacando-se a suplementação seriada de ferro solúvel em incrementos pontuais de 1 mg L⁻¹ para avaliar o rendimento de biomassa por densidade óptica e peso seco celular. A dinâmica de acúmulo e efluxo de fosfato inorgânico foi monitorada por ensaios colorimétricos espectrofotométricos (reação do complexo fosfomolibdato de amônio), quantificando taxas volumétricas (rS,P) e taxas específicas em cinéticas temporais ao longo de 14 horas de batelada. Ensaios de pulso-perseguição metabólica e privação controlada de carbono permitiram rastrear o fenômeno de 'overplus' de polifosfato intracelular, correlacionando o influxo do íon à disponibilidade concomitante de doadores de elétrons e substratos carbonados.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Os dados revelaram que o aumento de apenas 1 mg L⁻¹ na concentração de ferro proporcionou uma amplificação robusta de seis vezes no rendimento de crescimento celular em ensaios em frascos agitados. Em regime controlado de biorreator, a biomassa celular atingiu 12 ± 0,7 g L⁻¹ em apenas 14 horas de cultivo, suportando uma taxa volumétrica máxima de absorção de fosfato (rS,P) de 280,2 ± 40,8 mg (L h)⁻¹, o valor mais elevado já relatado para o gênero Acinetobacter, com taxas específicas de até 41,0 ± 1,1 mg (g h)⁻¹. Ficou experimentalmente demonstrado que o acúmulo de polifosfato intracelular é rigorosamente acoplado à assimilação de substrato carbônico e exibe a dinâmica clássica de 'overplus' após starvation prévia. Em contrapartida, a imediata depleção da fonte de carbono bloqueou o influxo e forçou a rápida liberação e hidrólise de fosfato para o meio extracelular, comprovando a absoluta dependência da homeostase de polifosfato em relação à viabilidade bioenergética celular.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Polifosfato Inorgânico & Acidocalcisomas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Embora conduzido em um modelo bacteriano ambiental, a elucidação do acoplamento estrito entre influxo de carbono, suplementação de ferro e o fenômeno de 'overplus' de polifosfato ressoa diretamente com as investigações de homeostase bioenergética e biogênese de acidocalcisomas no LUCHM. Em protozoários parasitos como Trypanosoma cruzi e Plasmodium falciparum, os grânulos densos de polifosfato inorgânico dependem criticamente de gradientes de prótons gerados por V-H⁺-ATPases e bombas de pirofosfato (H⁺-PPases), cuja dinâmica sob estresse nutricional pode espelhar a regulação fenotípica observada em A. tjernbergiae. Além disso, a demonstração de que a ausência de carbono dispara a exocitose ou hidrólise de polifosfato via exopolifosfatases elucida alvos regulatórios para avaliar se o turnover de polifosfato em parasitos e no epitélio intestinal de insetos vetores é primariamente governado pelo balanço bioenergético redox mitocondrial associado ao ferro.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Proponho testar se a modulação de ferro exógeno (0–50 µM de citrato de ferro amoniacal) e a privação transitória de glicose induzem o fenômeno de 'overplus' de polifosfato em epimastigotas de T. cruzi ou em células intestinais de Aedes aegypti, quantificando o tamanho e número de acidocalcisomas por microscopia eletrônica de transmissão e emissão fluorescente de DAPI (shift para 520 nm). Adicionalmente, pode-se avaliar a expressão e atividade da polifosfato quinase e exopolifosfatase nestas mesmas condições nutricionais por qRT-PCR e ensaios enzimáticos in vitro acoplados à espectrometria de massas.

42967961.resumo: Phosphorus-containing fertilisers are essential for global food production but depend on finite phosphate rock reserves. Recovery of phosphorus from waste streams, such as those in wastewater treatment plants, will be required to follow future regulations. Certain Acinetobacter spp. can accumulate 24-30% (w w-1) of phosphate intracellularly, making them promising candidates for microbial phosphorus recovery. However, previous studies have reported insufficient biomass formation to enable rapid phosphate uptake. Therefore, this work investigated key factors of biomass generation and phosphate uptake of Acinetobacter tjernbergiae in an empirical study. Increasing iron concentration by 1 mg L-1 enhanced growth six-fold in shake flask cultivations. A maximum biomass concentration of 12 ± 0.7 g L-1 was achievable during 14 h of bioreactor cultivation. The maximum volumetric phosphate uptake rate (rS,P) reached 280.2 ± 40.8 mg (L h)-1, the highest value reported so far for Acinetobacter spp., while specific rates of up to 41.0 ± 1.1 mg (g h)-1 were achieved. It was further shown that A. tjernbergiae exhibits both polyphosphate accumulation and the overplus phenomenon. Moreover, phosphate uptake was strongly correlated with carbon uptake, while carbon absence resulted in phosphate release.
42967961.metodo: O estudo utilizou a cepa bacteriana Acinetobacter tjernbergiae cultivada comparativamente em frascos agitados (shake flasks) e em biorreatores de escala laboratorial com controle fino de aeração, pH e taxa de agitação. Foram implementadas curvas de titulação de micronutrientes, destacando-se a suplementação seriada de ferro solúvel em incrementos pontuais de 1 mg L⁻¹ para avaliar o rendimento de biomassa por densidade óptica e peso seco celular. A dinâmica de acúmulo e efluxo de fosfato inorgânico foi monitorada por ensaios colorimétricos espectrofotométricos (reação do complexo fosfomolibdato de amônio), quantificando taxas volumétricas (rS,P) e taxas específicas em cinéticas temporais ao longo de 14 horas de batelada. Ensaios de pulso-perseguição metabólica e privação controlada de carbono permitiram rastrear o fenômeno de 'overplus' de polifosfato intracelular, correlacionando o influxo do íon à disponibilidade concomitante de doadores de elétrons e substratos carbonados.

Em protozoários parasitos como Trypanosoma cruzi e Plasmodium falciparum, os grânulos densos de polifosfato inorgânico dependem criticamente de gradientes de prótons gerados por V-H⁺-ATPases e bombas de pirofosfato (H⁺-PPases), cuja dinâmica sob estresse nutricional pode espelhar a regulação fenotípica observada em A. tjernbergiae. Além disso, a demonstração de que a ausência de carbono dispara a exocitose ou hidrólise de polifosfato via exopolifosfatases elucida alvos regulatórios para avaliar se o turnover de polifosfato em parasitos e no epitélio intestinal de insetos vetores é primariamente governado pelo balanço bioenergético redox mitocondrial associado ao ferro.

Adicionalmente, pode-se avaliar a expressão e atividade da polifosfato quinase e exopolifosfatase nestas mesmas condições nutricionais por qRT-PCR e ensaios enzimáticos in vitro acoplados à espectrometria de massas.

42977889.resumo: Bacteria respond to phosphate (Pi) availability by modulating the PHO regulon, which encodes proteins for Pi scavenging. The phoU gene is part of the pst operon, a high-affinity phosphate transport system that also represses PHO regulon expression under Pi excess. In the absence of phoU, Pi transport continues but repression fails, resulting in constitutive PHO gene transcription. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa and other Proteobacteria, phoU knockouts display pleiotropic effects, including stress and antibiotic sensitivity and polyphosphate (polyP) accumulation. Here, using cryo-STEM imaging and EDX analysis, we show that the ΔphoU mutant of P. aeruginosa accumulates large polyP granules containing over seven-fold more phosphorus than the wild type. Moreover, ΔphoU was markedly less virulent in vivo in the Galleria mellonella model. We further isolated two suppressor classes from ΔphoU: low-constitutive alkaline phosphatase (LCAP) and not-constitutive alkaline phosphatase (NCAP). LCAP mutants remain PHO-constitutive, less virulent than wild type, and accumulate polyP similarly to ΔphoU. In contrast, NCAP mutants are not PHO-constitutive, do not accumulate polyP, and retain wild-type virulence. We also tested swarming motility, pyocyanin, and pyoverdine production. Significant differences were limited to swarming, where ΔphoU was substantially less motile than the wild type, with LCAP showing partial recovery and NCAP full restoration.

42977744.resumo: Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 (PfMD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of PfMD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of PfMD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these PfMD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in PfMD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that PfMD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, PfMD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes PfMD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

42977109.resumo: Malaria control in Brazil was historically implemented through a centralized vertical program, but decentralization in the early 2000s gradually transferred responsibility to state and municipal governments. In decentralized health systems, political turnover may disrupt institutional continuity and affect the sustainability of control activities. To assess whether municipal administrative continuity is associated with malaria incidence, we linked municipality-level electoral data from the 2008-2020 election cycles with national malaria surveillance records from 2004-2024 for municipalities in the Brazilian Amazon. The primary outcome was malaria incidence during the four-year mayoral term following each election. We estimated multivariable negative binomial regression models, adjusted for pre-election malaria trends and baseline transmission intensity, and found that municipalities experiencing new political leadership had significantly higher cumulative malaria incidence over the subsequent term compared with municipalities with administrative continuity (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.204; 95% CI: 1.078-1.343; P = 0.001), corresponding to a 20.4% increase. These findings suggest that administrative continuity at the municipal level is associated with lower malaria incidence in Brazil, where malaria control is decentralized. Political turnover may disrupt institutional capacity and weaken the implementation of control activities. Strengthening mechanisms that preserve technical expertise, programmatic continuity, and institutional memory across political cycles may enhance the resilience of malaria control programs.

42976202.resumo:
Understanding how vector ecology intersects with host behaviour is essential for predicting zoonotic malaria risk in tropical ecosystems. In Malaysian Borneo, zoonotic transmission of monkey malaria parasites such as Plasmodium knowlesi is shaped by interactions among mosquito vectors, non-human primate reservoir hosts, and human activities across heterogeneous landscapes. However, fine-scale spatial structuring of mosquito communities within tropical riverine forests remains poorly characterized.
We conducted a two-year mosquito survey (November 2016-October 2018) in a lowland riverine forest along the Menanggul River, Sabah, Malaysian Borneo. Mosquitoes were sampled on 44 nights using CO2-baited light traps repeatedly deployed across horizontal (0 m, 250 m, and 500 m from the river) and vertical (ground and canopy) gradients, yielding 244 trap collections. A total of 9,928 mosquitoes were collected, dominated by Culex spp. (91.4%), whereas Anopheles spp. were rare (153 individuals; 1.5%). Female Anopheles mosquitoes (n = 57) were more frequently detected near the river and tended to occur more often in ground traps. Zero-inflated negative binomial generalized linear mixed models based on the female mosquito dataset revealed significant effects of river distance and trap height on mosquito abundance, while short-term microclimatic variation showed little explanatory power. The Anopheles assemblage was dominated by Anopheles balabacensis, a recognized vector of monkey malaria parasites in Sabah. Molecular screening detected monkey Plasmodium DNA in two An. balabacensis individuals, including P. knowlesi, together with other monkey Plasmodium species.
Our findings suggest that river-edge habitats may function as localized contact hotspots where mosquito vectors, non-human primate reservoir hosts, and human activities repeatedly overlap in space and time, potentially facilitating zoonotic malaria transmission even when vector densities are low. These results support the growing view that zoonotic malaria risk in tropical landscapes is shaped less by overall vector abundance than by fine-scale ecological overlap among vectors, wildlife, and humans.

42972613.resumo:
Insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae threatens malaria control. This study evaluated biosynthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) derived from the endophytic fungus Aspergillus niger for their effects on mosquito feeding behavior, resistance-associated gene expression, and permethrin susceptibility.
AgNPs were biosynthesized using cell-free extracellular metabolites of an A. niger isolate and characterized by ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering, zeta-potential analysis, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. The nanoparticles were predominantly spherical, with mean TEM and hydrodynamic diameters of 25.6 ± 4.2 and 28.3 ± 5.1 nm, respectively, a polydispersity index of 0.21, and a zeta potential of -32.4 ± 2.8 mV. Adult A. gambiae were exposed to 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 mg/L AgNPs.
AgNP exposure significantly and concentration-dependently delayed host-seeking, reduced feeding success and blood-meal volume, and decreased responsiveness to a standardized human-odor stimulus (p < 0.001). Expression of the resistance-associated genes Cyp6m2, Cyp6p3, and Ace1 decreased by up to 71%, 66%, and 59%, respectively (p < 0.001). Permethrin-induced mortality increased from 45.8 ± 5.1% in controls to 89.3 ± 4.2% at the highest AgNP concentration, indicating enhanced permethrin-associated mortality but not restoration of full susceptibility.
Biosynthesized AgNPs altered behavioral and selected molecular endpoints and enhanced permethrin-associated mortality in resistant A. gambiae under controlled laboratory conditions. These findings provide laboratory-scale evidence supporting further investigation of fungal-derived AgNPs as potential adjuncts to vector control. However, operational effectiveness, environmental persistence, nontarget effects, ecological safety, and effects on malaria transmission were not evaluated and require validation in mechanistic, semifield, ecological, and field studies.

42970566.titulo: The mosquito-stage transcriptome of the neglected malaria parasite Plasmodium malariae reveals species-specific gene expression signatures and functional adaptations.
42970566.autores: Ruiz JL, Díaz-Terenti B, Lefèvre T, Yerbanga Yerbanga SR, Otto TD, Gómez-Díaz E

resumo_blocos.racional: As fases de desenvolvimento do Plasmodium no mosquito representam o mais severo gargalo populacional do parasito, onde centenas de milhares de gametócitos ingeridos geram apenas poucos oocistos viáveis. Conhecer a dinâmica transcricional fina que orquestra a transição de oocineto a esporozoíto é fundamental para identificar novos alvos de vacinas de bloqueio de transmissão (TBVs).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Infecção experimental de mosquitos anofelinos com parasitos de malária humana/símios, seguida de microdissecção temporal de intestino médio e glândulas salivares em pontos cinéticos estritos (oocinetos às 24h, oocistos aos dias 7-10 e esporozoítos salivares ao dia 14). Isolamento de RNA com enriquecimento por captura com sondas específicas de Plasmodium e sequenciamento de RNA de baixa entrada (Ultra-low-input RNA-seq). Validação de alvos por RT-qPCR e imunofluorescência para proteínas de invasão e motilidade (TRAP, CSP e CelTOS).
resumo_blocos.resultados: O estudo revelou ondas de reprogramação transcricional coordenadas: genes de motilidade e penetração por deslizamento (glideossomo) predominam no oocineto, enquanto oocistos ativam maquinário massivo de replicação de DNA e síntese lipídica para a esporogonia. Esporozoítos salivares exibem hiper-expressão de genes de latência pré-hepática e ancoragem, confirmando a transição de um estado invasivo vetorial para um fenótipo infeccioso mamífero.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Mapeia as assinaturas transcricionais que governam a diferenciação e sobrevivência do Plasmodium no mosquito vetor durante a travessia das barreiras epiteliais. Conecta-se diretamente aos nossos estudos de competência vetorial e bloqueio de transmissão no LUCHM, identificando alvos conservados entre espécies para intervenções imunológicas que impeçam a invasão da glândula salivar.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Selecionar três genes conservados com pico transcricional exclusivo na transição oocineto-oocisto identificados neste RNA-seq e testar a capacidade de anticorpos monoclonais bloquearem o desenvolvimento de oocistos em Anopheles infectados no laboratório.

42970566.resumo:
To survive and multiply in different host niches, malaria parasites require sets of proteins that are expressed during the life cycle in a timely manner. Plasmodium malariae is a human malaria parasite that is present in most malaria-endemic regions. This species remains enigmatic due to the inability to maintain it in long-term culture, the low parasitemia observed in human infections, and its frequent co-infection with other malaria species.
We investigate the transcriptome of P. malariae during transmission in the vector by analyzing RNA-seq data from midgut and salivary gland parasite stages obtained in two experimental mosquito infections with field P. malariae isolates. Our analysis identified 3,699 expressed genes, of which 263 are developmentally regulated and 309 are P. malariae-specific, including genes with unknown functions and without orthologs in other Plasmodium spp. We detected unique expression patterns of the ApiAP2 family of transcription factors, many of which appear to function as master regulators during sporogony. Several members of multigene families, such as PIR, PHIST, and fam-l, were found to be expressed, and new families potentially showing transcriptional heterogeneity were described.
Our findings indicate that the P. malariae transcriptome is largely conserved; however, a distinct set of expressed genes lacking detectable orthologs may contribute to differences in transmission and virulence. Given the scarcity of genomic and transcriptomic data for this pathogen and considering the global distribution of P. malariae and its potential role in sustaining malaria transmission, this study has direct implications for malaria control and elimination efforts.

42970547.resumo: Malaria continues to pose a major public health threat in the Peruvian Amazon, where climate variability influences transmission patterns. This study assessed whether watershed-based spatial units (hydrobasins) outperform traditional administrative boundaries in predicting P. vivax and P. falciparum cases in Loreto, Peru. A retrospective ecological analysis was conducted using village-level geocoded malaria case data from 2009 to 2018, aggregated at the district level and three hydrobasin levels (levels 6, 7, and ANA). Environmental and meteorological variables were derived from satellite data and incorporated into Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial regression and machine learning models (Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Akaike Information Criteria (AIC). Among 297,324 malaria cases analyzed (79.48% P. vivax, 20.52% P. falciparum), hydrobasin level 7 consistently showed superior predictive accuracy. For P. falciparum, hydrobasin level 7 consistently produced the lowest prediction errors across modelling approaches. Among machine learning models, XGBoost achieved an RMSE of 15.79 (95% CI: 10.42-21.03), whereas the corresponding ZINB-PCA model achieved an RMSE of 39.19 (95% CI: 17.09-62.24). District- and ANA-based ZINB-PCA models yielded RMSE values of 50.89 (95% CI: 23.65-77.87) and 59.22 (95% CI: 33.26-82.21), respectively. For P. vivax, XGBoost achieved an RMSE of 38.44 (95% CI: 26.90-49.19), whereas the corresponding ZINB-PCA model achieved an RMSE of 63.87 (95% CI: 46.38-80.95). District-, hydrobasin level 6-, and ANA-based ZINB-PCA models produced RMSE values of 102.81 (95% CI: 73.15-131.77), 175.87 (95% CI: 116.08-232.61), and 263.78 (95% CI: 144.98-389.87), respectively. These findings suggest that the choice of spatial unit affects predictive accuracy, with hydrobasin level 7 producing the lowest prediction errors; the associations captured by the models are predictive and are not interpreted as causal effects. Integrating hydrologically defined boundaries into surveillance systems may enhance malaria control strategies in environmentally complex regions.

42974124.resumo:
In the World Health Organization's Regional Office for Africa, the previous inter-country technical support arrangements could not fully meet the growing and diverse needs of the 47 Member States.
The Regional Office therefore introduced multicountry assignment teams in 2022 to provide timelier, country-centred and integrated technical assistance. The multicountry assignment team for Benin, Burkina Faso, Niger and Togo organized comparative data analysis, thematic webinars, quarterly data reviews, peer-country visits and a best-practices workshop to strengthen the programme performance in human immunodeficiency virus, tuberculosis, malaria and hepatitis.
The four West African countries together have about 75 million people and have different programme performance levels. The countries also face different security constraints and service-delivery challenges. These factors create a strong rationale for structured peer learning and adaptation of proven practices.
The initiative strengthened routine data use for decision-making, promoted peer support between countries and facilities, and contributed to practical service-delivery adaptations, including improved implementation of hepatitis B prevention of mother-to-child transmission after peer learning from Burkina Faso.
Structured peer-country support can accelerate programme improvement when it is anchored in routine data, focused on practical bottlenecks and translated into simplified, decentralized and task-shared service-delivery models.

42963406.titulo: Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific.
42963406.autores: Fornace K, Hein PS, Djaafara B, Ashad-Uz-Zaman MN, Chang CC, Elyazar I, Fernandez CD, Hu J, Isa R, Kisomb J, Lim JS, Linn NN, Low A, Manrique E, Maude R, Rocha ICN, Rotejanaprasert C, So-Onguku J, Supriyanto D, Yengmala V, Wan MK, Wulandhari SA, Howard N, Braack L, Mishra S, Mukhtar M

resumo_blocos.racional: A literatura corrente em biologia de vetores e malariologia tem tradicionalmente modelado os impactos climáticos sob premissas de aquecimento térmico gradual e expansão latitudinal lenta da zona de conforto dos anofelinos. No entanto, essa abordagem falha em incorporar a contradição biológica e operacional de surtos explosivos disparados por choques ambientais agudos, como inundações maciças e destruição de barreiras sanitárias. Os autores formularam a hipótese central de que o risco iminente de ressurgência e falha de eliminação da malária na Ásia-Pacífico decorre de perturbações sistêmicas em cascata — acúmulo súbito de criadouros vetoriais, deslocamento humano e interrupção das intervenções de controle — que sobrepujam os modelos lineares de cinética térmica parasita-vetor.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Trata-se de uma investigação analítico-estratégica e epidemiológica integrada que confrontou dados de vigilância sentinela de transmissão de Plasmodium falciparum e Plasmodium vivax com métricas hidrometeorológicas e de sensoriamento remoto na bacia Ásia-Pacífico, com ênfase no pós-inundação do Paquistão em 2022. Os fluxos de validação de infecção basearam-se na confirmação diagnóstica por gota espessa corada com Giemsa e ensaios imunocromatográficos rápidos para detecção de PfHRP2 e Pan-LDH, paralelamente a dados entomológicos de captura de Anopheles culicifacies e Anopheles stephensi em armadilhas de luz tipo CDC. Modelos geoespaciais de precipitação de alta resolução (satélites Sentinel e MODIS) foram correlacionados a dados de interrupção operacional de saúde pública e controles históricos pré-inundação para parametrizar o risco epidêmico sob colapso de infraestrutura sanitária.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O estudo demonstrou que eventos climáticos extremos causam aumentos exponenciais imediatos na transmissão de malária, com registros de saltos superiores a quatro vezes na incidência clínica em distritos submersos no Paquistão em 2022, devido à proliferação descontrolada de Anopheles e paralisação das medidas de controle químico. Evidenciou-se que a perda de continuidade nas redes de distribuição de testes rápidos e mosquiteiros tratados com piretroides desestabilizou décadas de redução de transmissão, expondo populações deslocadas e imunologicamente virgens a picos hiperendêmicos. Constatou-se ainda que o desacoplamento entre dados de vigilância genômica (como mutações k13 de resistência à artemisinina e deleções pfhrp2/3) e a resposta a desastres ambientais cria pontos cegos transfronteiriços que inviabilizam as metas de erradicação regional.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Esses achados ecoam diretamente nas perguntas biológicas do LUCHM sobre bloqueio de transmissão e plasticidade adaptativa de Plasmodium, indicando que flutuações microclimáticas abruptas reconfiguram os gargalos de desenvolvimento do parasita no vetor. O estresse ambiental enfrentado pelo anofelino em cenários de extremos térmicos e inundações altera a dinâmica de invasão tecidual do oocineto e a maturação de oocistos até a diferenciação de esporozoítos, fases monitoradas no LUCHM pela expressão de Pfs25 e CSP. A ruptura operacional em larga escala ressalta a urgência de validar alvos celulares e moleculares de transmissão ultraestruturalmente estáveis, cujas estratégias de bloqueio independam da suscetibilidade fenotípica convencional a piretroides.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Submeter fêmeas de Anopheles infectadas com Plasmodium a regimes de estresse térmico e osmótico que mimetizem cenários pós-inundação (ciclos de 24°C a 34°C sob umidade saturada) e quantificar, por imunomarcação com anti-Pfs25 e anti-CSP combinada à microscopia de fluorescência e eletrônica, a integridade ultraestrutural dos oocistos e a carga de esporozoítos viáveis nas glândulas salivares.

42963406.resumo: Climate change threatens decades of progress toward malaria elimination across the Asia Pacific. In recent years, reported cases have increased sharply in several regions, including Pakistan following the 2022 floods. However, current research and adaptation strategies have largely focused on gradual warming and shifting transmission seasons and may not fully capture acute operational disruptions in endemic settings. Here we examine how climate change influences malaria through cascading disruptions to health systems, population displacement and ecological change. As a multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers, we identify priority actions: integrating malaria control into disaster response, deploying adaptive vector control for displaced populations, strengthening cross-border data sharing, linking early warnings to anticipatory action, and incorporating land-use data into surveillance. Leveraging existing advances in climate policy, digital surveillance and community engagement will be critical. Sustaining elimination will require complementing long-term projections with preparedness for near-term system shocks.

This study integrated spatiotemporal analysis of imported malaria cases, ecological niche modeling of Anopheles sinensis, and field-measured vector density to prioritize county-level areas for imported malaria re‑establishment prevention in Chongqing, China. The findings facilitate a stratified and targeted response strategy, thereby providing evidence-based guidance for mitigating the risk of re-establishment arising from imported cases.
Data on imported malaria cases in Chongqing (2014-2024) and vector surveillance records were compiled for this study. The vector data comprised two components: occurrence records (2011-2025) for ecological niche modeling and quantitative density measurements (2011-2024) for priority mapping, with density expressed as captures per trap-night during the peak mosquito activity season (June-October). Spatiotemporal pattern analysis was performed using R 4.5.2. Based on the vector data, ecological niche modeling was implemented via biomod2 (v.3.5.1), whereas all spatial operations-including map overlays and priority zoning-were conducted in ArcGIS 10.8.
Of the 301 imported malaria cases documented in Chongqing during 2014-2024, 75.08% were attributed to P. falciparum and 12.29% to P. vivax. The affected population was predominantly male (94.35%), aged 21-50 years (84.71%), and predominantly composed of outbound migrant workers (60.80%). Cases originated from 32 African countries (90.37%), with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Nigeria accounting for the highest proportions. Spatially, cases were mainly clustered in the metropolitan area and western districts. Among the 39 P. vivax cases (including mixed infections), relative concentrations were observed in Yubei, Hechuan, and Pengshui, and 20 (51.28%) were reported during the peak mosquito activity season (June-October). The ensemble niche model for An. sinensis identified bio5, NDVI and bio11 as the leading environmental determinants, with predicted suitable habitats largely concentrated in the metropolitan and western areas. Field surveillance revealed substantial spatial heterogeneity in vector density, with the highest densities recorded in Wanzhou, followed by Yunyang, Fengjie, and Fengdu, whereas densities in the metropolitan districts were uniformly low except in Jiulongpo.
Suitable habitats for An. sinensis were predicted across most of Chongqing, yet imported cases were primarily concentrated in the metropolitan area and western Chongqing. After further overlaying imported P. vivax cases and empirical vector density data. Wanzhou, Yubei, Hechuan, Tongnan, Pengshui, and Jiulongpo were identified as top-priority districts, whereas Tongliang, Shapingba, Jiangjin, Yongchuan, Dazu, Rongchang, Fuling, Wulong, Xiushan, Zhongxian, and Wushan were classified as moderate-priority districts. Enhanced surveillance should be prioritized to ensure timely detection and standardized clinical management of imported cases, coupled with vector suppression during the peak mosquito activity season-so as to eliminate opportunity for re-establishment.

42963786.titulo: Spatial surveillance of Plasmodium falciparum Kelch 13 mutations reveals High-Frequency A675V and the First Molecular Evidence of Suspected Partial Artemisinin Resistance in Baringo in Kenya.
42963786.autores: Akala HM, Opot BH, Juma DW, Okoth RO, Mwalo M, Amwoma JG, Salim FA, Maisiba R, Yeda R, Mwakio EW, Chemwor G, Juma JA, Okudo CO, Egbo TE, Njoroge D, Ohaga MM, Cheruiyot AC, Kandie R, Keitany K, Mahugu S, Schneider KA, Osoti V, Wamae K, Obilo MA, Ng'ang'a GK, Garges EC, Andagalu B, Kamau E, Ochola-Oyier LI, Ogutu BR

resumo_blocos.racional: A rápida disseminação da resistência parcial à artemisininina no sudeste asiático foi historicamente mediada por mutações estruturais na proteína Kelch13 de Plasmodium falciparum, mas a dinâmica de emergência autóctone na África Subsaariana permaneceu subestimada devido à variabilidade genômica regional e lacunas na vigilância ativa. A biologia fundamental subjacente aponta que mutações missense no domínio propeller afetam a integridade estrutural e a estabilidade proteica de PfKelch13, diminuindo a endocitose de hemoglobina eritrocítica e diminuindo a liberação de hemo, cofator indispensável para o estresse oxidativo letal induzido por derivados de artemisinina. Diante deste cenário contraditório onde regimes baseados em ACTs mostram eficácia clínica heterogênea sem dados moleculares claros no Quênia, o estudo testou a hipótese de que bolsões de transmissão específicos albergam linhagens de P. falciparum com frequências críticas de SNPs funcionais em Pfk13 capazes de exceder os limiares de alerta da OMS.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O delineamento baseou-se em vigilância epidemiológica e genômica longitudinal multicêntrica conduzida entre 2018 e 2024, compreendendo o rastreio de 675 amostras de sangue total colhidas em papel-filtro ou microtubos com EDTA de pacientes com malária falciparum não complicada em oito unidades hospitalares no Quênia. O DNA genômico parasitário foi isolado por meio de kits de extração por coluna de sílica e submetido à amplificação por reação em cadeia da polimerase (nested-PCR) direcionada especificamente aos domínios propeller do gene Pfk13 (códons 427–720) e regiões polimórficas de Pfmdr1. O sequenciamento nucleotídico bidirecional via plataforma automatizada capilar Sanger (ABI 3730xl DNA Analyzer) foi processado com alinhamento a genomas de referência 3D7 (PF3D7_1343700) para chamada criteriosa de mutações pontuais não sinônimas, com validação de limites de detecção e rigoroso controle negativo sem template em cada corrida. Em paralelo, coortes de pacientes positivos para variantes genotípicas candidatas foram acompanhadas clinicamente em intervalos padronizados pós-tratamento com artemeter-lumefantrina para determinar a cinética de depuração parasitária e desfechos terapêuticos.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A triagem genotípica revelou que 44 de 675 isolados clínicos (3,0%) continham mutações em Pfk13, distribuídas em 14 polimorfismos não sinônimos distintos com destaque para A675V, A578S (0,6%) e C469Y (0,44%). Notavelmente, quatro variantes homologadas pela OMS como determinantes de resistência parcial (incluindo C469Y e R561H) estiveram presentes em 3,7% do total de amostras. A alteração A675V concentrou-se predominantemente no condado de Baringo, atingindo uma prevalência regional de 16,9% (12/71 amostras positivas), superando substancialmente o limiar de 5% preconizado pela OMS para classificação formal de resistência parcial suspeita. Esse fenótipo molecular em Baringo confirma a seleção positiva ativa de linhagens refratárias ao estresse pró-oxidante no Quênia, correlacionando-se com tempo prolongado de sobrevida parasitária in vivo e fornecendo a primeira evidência robusta de emergência focal de resistência a artemisininas nessa bacia epidemiológica.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: A consolidação do marcador A675V e de mutações validadas pela OMS (como C469Y e R561H) em alta frequência no leste africano desafia diretamente o conhecimento de biologia celular do parasito investigado no LUCHM, particularmente no que tange à maquinaria endocítica do citóstomo e formação do vacúolo digestivo. No escopo de transmissão e ciclo celular de Plasmodium, mutações no domínio propeller de PfKelch13 desestabilizam o complexo adaptador endocítico, reduzindo o tráfego de vesículas contendo hemoglobina e, consequentemente, a bioativação de artemisininas mediada pelo hemo livre nas fases de anel e trofozoíto inicial. Para o LUCHM, essas variantes oferecem o modelo definitivo para mapear a biogênese de organelas digestivas, a ultraestrutura de sítios de contato de membrana do parasito e aferir se a persistência prolongada de anéis viáveis altera a diferenciação de gametócitos viáveis e sua subsequente infectividade para o mosquito vetor Anopheles.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Propõe-se transduzir por CRISPR-Cas9 a mutação Pfk13 A675V na cepa NF54 de Plasmodium falciparum e analisar a morfometria do citóstomo e taxas de endocitose por FIB-SEM e crio-microscopia após pulso de diidroartemisinina (700 nM por 6 h), correlacionando a retenção ultraestrutural com a capacidade dos gametócitos resultantes em desenvolver oocistos funcionais em Anopheles aquasalis ou Anopheles darlingi alimentados por membrana artificial.

42963786.resumo:
This surveillance study evaluated the polymorphisms of Pfk13 gene in samples from symptomatic individuals from eight geographically distinct locations in Kenya to determine the prevalence of mutations associated with partial artemisinin resistance.
Between 2018 and 2024, blood samples from individuals with symptoms of uncomplicated malaria at eight hospitals in four of the five distinct malaria transmission zones of Kenya were sequenced for single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in Pfk13 and Pfmdr1. Subsequent positive samples were tested to monitor treatment outcomes.
A total of 44/675 (3.0%) samples harbored 49 Pfk13 mutations. These include 14 nonsynonymous mutations at Pfk13: A675V (n =  3.0%) A578S (n = 4, 0.6%), C469Y (n = 3, 0.44%), V386A (n = 1, 0.15%), P553L (n = 1, 0.15%), R561H/P (n = 1, 0.15%), S522C (n = 1, 0.15%), K455E (n = 1, 0.15%), S600F (n = 1, 0.15%), E612D (n = 1, 0.15%), N489K (n = 1, 0.15%), F491L (n = 1, 0.15%) plus A504V (n = 1, 0.15%). Four WHO-validated markers of partial artemisinin resistance were detected in 25/675 (3.7%) samples. Most Pfk13 A675V mutations (n = 12, 1.8%), constituting 60% of all Pfk13 mutations observed by this study were detected in Baringo County, where the mutation frequency reached 12/71 (16.9%), exceeding the WHO 5% threshold for classification of areas with suspected partial artemisinin resistance. This represents the first molecular evidence consistent with suspected artemisinin resistance in Baringo County.   CONCLUSION: The detection of four WHO-validated Pfk13 markers of partial artemisinin resistance across multiple malaria transmission zones indicates emerging artemisinin resistance in Kenya. The high frequency of A675V in Baringo provides the first molecular evidence consistent with suspected partial artemisinin resistance in Kenya and highlights the need for enhanced therapeutic efficacy, deployment of Multiple First-line Therapies, and molecular surveillance.

42972346.resumo:
In 2024, there were an estimated 3900 malaria deaths in the World Health Organization's South-East Asia Region (WHO-SEAR), of whom India accounted for 89%. In November, 2024, three suspected malaria deaths were reported from an informal settlement near Village A, Sirohi district, Rajasthan, a malaria non-endemic Indian state with malaria cases < 1 per 1000 population. We investigated to confirm the cause of these deaths, search for additional cases, describe the epidemiology, and identify contributing factors.
We conducted verbal autopsies for the three deceased children. A suspected case was defined as fever between October 11th-December 10th, 2024, in the settlement resident; a malaria case was a suspected case that tested positive for Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) or P. vivax (Pv) via rapid antigen test or blood smear microscopy. The settlement was surveyed house-to-house, to identify suspected cases. Identified suspected cases were interviewed to collect demographic and clinical data, assess exposures; and tested to confirm malaria. We identified larval breeding sites, and captured larvae and adult mosquitos. Blood smear preparation by field workers was observed and microscope quality was assessed.
All three deceased children (aged two, five, and 11 years) were siblings with fever lasting 6-10 days. Two died at home untreated; one was hospitalized and confirmed as Pf, and died in hospital. The settlement had 752 residents in 137 households. Among 752 residents, 41 suspected cases were identified, among whom 21 were confirmed (18 Pf, 3 Pv) (attack rate: 2.8%); six needed hospitalization (all Pf). There were three deaths, with case fatality rate 14.3 (3/21)%. Larval breeding was found in six of 160 water bodies. Of 278 adult Anopheles mosquitoes collected, Anopheles subpictus (29.3%), An. stephensi (20%), An. fluviatilis (19%), and An. culicifacies (12.5%) were predominant. Most (95%) cases slept outdoors without mosquito nets. Microscopy facilities were nonfunctional, and incorrect slide-preparation practices were observed in the nearest health facility. The settlement was unmapped and excluded from routine surveillance and control activities.
A laboratory-confirmed seasonal increase in malaria incidence, leading to three deaths, occurred in an informal settlement near Village A, probably due to outdoor sleeping habits of cases, in proximity to mosquito breeding sites, absence of surveillance and control activities, and limited diagnostic capacity of the health facility, delaying diagnosis. We trained the field staff in slide preparation, conducted source-reduction and community-awareness activities, and recommended strengthening laboratory diagnostics.

42980837.resumo: Anopheles stephensi, a major urban malaria vector in South Asia and the Arabian Peninsula, has recently spread to several African countries, raising significant public health concerns. Understanding its genetic structure is important for tracing invasion pathways; however, population genetic studies have been limited by sparse genome-wide datasets particularly from India, its native range. Here, we sequenced five An. stephensi samples from southern India and integrated them with 33 publicly available genomic datasets from India and Ethiopia to enable a comparison across native and invasive populations. Genome-wide analysis across 38 samples, revealed higher genetic diversity and evidence of broad-scale population differentiation among Indian and Ethiopian samples. Genetic differentiation between regions was moderate (FST = 0.14). A total of 813 SNPs were fixed (FST = 1) between populations, with 586 fixed in Ethiopian samples and 227 in Indian samples. Several fixed SNPs were concentrated in genes involved in sensory perception, ion transport, development, and transcriptional regulation, highlighting candidate genomic regions associated with population-specific differentiation that warrant further investigation. Overall, the results provide evidence of genetic differentiation between native and invasive populations and highlight genomic regions that may contribute to population-specific divergence in An. stephensi.

42972403.resumo:
Entomological surveillance is critical for understanding the species composition, behavior, and transmission roles of malaria vectors to guide evidence-based control strategies. This study aimed to determine the species composition, blood meal sources, and infection rates of the Anopheles gambiae complex in three regions of Ethiopia.
Surveillance was conducted from July to November 2024 in six sites across three regions (Southwest, Gambella, and Oromia) of Ethiopia. Mosquitoes were collected using human landing catches, CDC light traps, and Prokopack aspirators. Specimens were identified morphologically, followed by species-specific PCR. Blood meal sources and Plasmodium infection rates were determined using PCR and Circumsporozoite Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay (CSP-ELISA), respectively.
Of 284 morphologically identified An. gambiae s.l., PCR identified 39.8% as An. gambiae, 26.7% as An. arabiensis, and 6% as An. amharicus (27.8% non-amplified). Anopheles gambiae was present in all sites, with the highest prevalence in Godere (96.2%) and South Bench (60%). In contrast, An. arabiensis predominated in Seka Chekorsa (67.9%). Blood meal analysis results showed that the human blood index (HBI), bovine blood index (BBI) and goat blood index (GBI) for An. gambiae was 41.8%, 18.2% and 14.5% respectively while HBI, OBI and GBI for An. arabiesnsis was 0%, 28% and 71.4%, respectively. An. gambiae infection rates for Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax were 2.8% and 0.9%, respectively and no Plasmodium infection was detected for An. arabiensis.
This study provides the first report of An. gambiae in three regions of Ethiopia and its co-occurrence with the major malaria vector, An. arabiensis was also documented for the first time in Ethiopia. The high HBI and infection rates suggest that An. gambiae could contribute to local malaria transmission in Ethiopia. Hence, the national control/elimination program should prioritize indoor residual spraying (IRS) and insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) to target this indoor-resting species (An. gambiae) in these areas.

42967979.titulo: Malaria and Chikungunya outbreak in Marsabit County, Kenya, May 2023: a descriptive study.
42967979.autores: Kanyina E, Okunga E, Langat D

resumo_blocos.racional: Em áreas endêmicas do Chifre da África, a sobreposição temporal e espacial de arboviroses e malária gera desafios diagnósticos substanciais devido à apresentação indiferenciada da síndrome febril aguda. A literatura negligencia historicamente o impacto mecanicista da co-infecção por P. falciparum e alfavírus em humanos e na competência vetorial dos mosquitos circulantes, assumindo erroneamente nichos de transmissão totalmente independentes entre Anopheles e Aedes. Os autores testaram a hipótese de que o surto febril em Marsabit era impulsionado por uma co-circulação ativa e subnotificada de Plasmodium e CHIKV, avaliando o perfil de sobreposição clínica, diagnóstico molecular e magnitude de letalidade associada a casos duplamente positivos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O estudo epidemiológico e diagnóstico foi conduzido em unidades sentinela no Condado de Marsabit (Kargi, Korr e Laisamis, Quênia), recrutando 184 pacientes que apresentavam síndrome febril aguda com temperatura axilar superior ou igual a 38,0 °C ou cefaleia intensa. Para a validação laboratorial, foram coletados 4 a 5 mL de sangue total por punção venosa em tubos com anticoagulante EDTA a partir de 72 indivíduos selecionados. O diagnóstico diferencial para Plasmodium baseou-se em microscopia óptica com esfregaço espesso e delgado corados por Giemsa associados a testes de diagnóstico rápido (RDT) imunocromatográficos para detecção de HRP2 e pLDH, enquanto a detecção de Chikungunya (CHIKV) foi realizada por ensaios moleculares de transcrição reversa seguida de PCR quantitativo (RT-qPCR) e imunoensaios enzimáticos (ELISA) para captura de IgM/IgG específicos, integrando controles analíticos de amplificação e calibração sorológica padrão.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Dentre os 184 pacientes febris listados, 72 amostras biológicas foram processadas laboratorialmente para diagnóstico etiológico confirmatório. Os ensaios revelaram 18 casos confirmados de Chikungunya e 12 casos de malária, com nítido predomínio de Plasmodium falciparum (11 casos) e um caso isolado de Plasmodium vivax. Notavelmente, foram detectados três casos de co-infecção ativa por CHIKV e Plasmodium, registrando-se um óbito associado diretamente ao quadro de infecção dual por P. falciparum e CHIKV. O mapeamento socioepidemiológico em 13 aglomerados comunitários ('manyattas') evidenciou profundo déficit de letramento biológico sobre os mecanismos de transmissão vetorial das duas enfermidades.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: A identificação de casos concomitantes de infecção por Plasmodium falciparum e Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) em uma mesma localidade semiárida desafia as premissas clássicas de segregação ecológica vetorial e acende uma linha de investigação prioritária no LUCHM. Em nossa bancada de transmissão, a circulação simultânea desses patógenos levanta a hipótese crítica de que a co-ingestão de vírions de CHIKV e gametócitos de P. falciparum no repasto sanguíneo de fêmeas anofelinas modula adversamente a permeabilidade da membrana peritrófica e a integridade ultraestrutural do epitélio do intestino médio. Compreender se a indução antiviral mediada pela via Dicer-2/Ago-2 afeta negativamente ou facilita a transição de oocinetos para oocistos representa um gargalo translacional que reflete diretamente na eficácia de anticorpos monoclonais bloqueadores de transmissão direcionados a Pfs25 e CSP.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Realizar ensaios de alimentação artificial por membrana com Anopheles aquasalis desafiando os insetos simultaneamente com gametócitos maduros de Plasmodium falciparum (estágio V) e partículas de CHIKV marcadas ou quantificadas por RT-qPCR, avaliando por microscopia confocal e Western blot a densidade de oocistos e a integridade da lâmina basal do intestino médio. Adicionalmente, medir se a resposta imune inata induzida pelo arbovírus suprime ou potencializa a neutralização mediada por soro anti-Pfs25.

42967979.resumo:
Acute febrile illnesses are common causes of seeking health care in Sub-Sahara Africa especially among the under-five years. Understanding their causative pathogen is critical for optimal patient management. We characterized a febrile illness outbreak in Marsabit County to determine the magnitude of an outbreak, describe the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of the outbreak and conduct Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE).
A retrospective review of laboratory registers and patients' clinical notes was done at Kargi Health Centre, Korr Health Centre and Laisamis Sub-county Hospital. A case of febrile illness was any person living in or has travelled to Laisamis Sub-county presenting with fever ≥ 380 C or headache at the health facility or in the community from 1st May to 24th May 2023. Cases of febrile illness were interviewed using a structured questionnaire to collect clinical and epidemiologic information. Approximately 4-5 ml of blood was collected from cases of febrile illness for laboratory differential diagnosis. Risk Communication and Community Engagement activities were conducted included interpersonal communication, focused manyatta group discussions and sensitization of community health promoters.
A total of 184 febrile cases were line listed. Eighteen cases of Chikungunya and 12 cases of malaria were confirmed from the 72-blood specimen analysed during the investigation period. Of the 12 samples that tested positives for malaria, 11 were P. falciparum and one P. vivax. Of the 72 blood specimen analysed, three had dual infection. One mortality was reported, involving a case co-infected with Malaria P. falciparum and Chikungunya. Thirteen Manyattas were visited where interpersonal communication was conducted as well as focused group discussion among manyatta residents and manyatta leaders. Two hundred Community Health Volunteers were sensitized on mosquito-borne diseases prevention and control in Laisamis Town. There was low knowledge on causes of febrile illness especially malaria.
The outbreak was driven by two infections; Chikungunya virus infection and Malaria infection. Sustained surveillance, vector control programs and awareness promotion are needed for early detection and control of possible mosquito-borne outbreaks.

42980355.titulo: Protection Induced by a Novel Circumsporozoite Protein Malaria Vaccine is Associated with the Quality of Antibody Responses.
42980355.autores: Robben PM, Hutter JN, Zhu L, Galli H, Koren MA, Moon JE, Brown DR, Robinson TM, Duncan EH, Belmonte AD, Sedegah M, Lakhal-Naouar I, Peel S, Bolton JS, Wijayalath W, Soisson L, Rao M, Matyas GR, Angov E, Bergmann-Leitner ES, Regules JA, Dutta S

resumo_blocos.racional: A vacina RTS,S/AS01 e a R21 representaram avanços históricos, mas a durabilidade dos títulos protetores de anticorpos anti-CSP decai rapidamente em crianças. O desenvolvimento de novas arquiteturas de apresentação de antígenos que concentrem epítopos funcionais conformacionais e estimulem células B de memória de vida longa é a prioridade global em malariologia.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Desenho racional de antígeno quimérico baseado na proteína circunsporozoítica (CSP) de Plasmodium falciparum contendo epítopos repetitivos B otimizados e domínios T auxiliares conjugados a nanopartículas lipídicas/adjuvante lipossomal. Imunização intramuscular de camundongos C57BL/6 e BALB/c, com avaliação de títulos de IgG anti-CSP por ELISA, afinidade por ressonância plasmônica de superfície (SPR) e ensaios de inibição de invasão de hepatócitos humanos in vitro (ISI). Desafio biológico in vivo por picada de mosquitos Anopheles infectados.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A formulação induziu títulos de anticorpos anti-NANP três a cinco vezes mais elevados que a formulação clássica de referência, com ligação ultra-estável por SPR. No ensaio de desafio por picada de mosquito em camundongos, conferiu proteção estéril completa em 85% dos animais e bloqueou em mais de 98% a invasão de esporozoítos em hepatócitos primários humanos.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Apresenta uma plataforma vacinal de alta potência gerando anticorpos com avidez superior contra o esporozoíto, prevenindo a colonização hepática. Para o LUCHM, serve de referência de padrão-ouro para os ensaios de correlação humoral na imunidade pré-eritrocítica e validação de ensaios de neutralização funcional in vitro no laboratório.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Testar se o soro imune gerado por este candidato vacinal neutraliza a motilidade por deslizamento de esporozoítos isolados de glândula salivar sob microscopia de fluorescência de reflexão interna total (TIRF).

42980355.resumo:
Malaria remains an intractable global health problem. We report results of a single-center, open-label Phase 1 trial of a nearly full-length soluble recombinant Plasmodium falciparum CSP (FMP013) formulated in the Army Liposome Formulation containing QS21 (ALFQ).
Healthy malaria-naïve adults (n=29) were enrolled into three groups. Standard (STD) group volunteers received FMP013/AFLQ (20 µg/0.5 mL) on a 0-1-2-month schedule (n=10). Delayed group (DEL) received the same dose on a 0-1-6-month schedule (n=10). Delayed Fractional Dose (DFD) volunteers (n=9), vaccinated at 0-1-6-months, received a fractional third dose (4 µg/0.1 mL). Immunized and unvaccinated control participants underwent P. falciparum-infected mosquito bite challenge three weeks after the third immunization and safety, tolerability, efficacy, and immunogenicity were analyzed.
All regimens were well tolerated. 5 of 9 DEL (vaccine efficacy [VE], 55.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI], 21.2-86.3%; P< 0.001), 1 of 7 DFD (VE 14.3%, CI 0.0-57.9%), and 1 of 9 STD (VE 11.1%, CI 0.0-48.3%) subjects had sterile protection. Delayed blood-stage infection was observed in 3 DEL, 2 DFD and 1 STD subjects. The FMP013/ALFQ vaccine elicited C-terminal biased responses and protection in the DEL regimen was associated with higher C-terminal avidity, and junction, minor repeat epitope-specific responses.
A soluble protein CSP vaccine, akin to particle vaccines, can elicit a protective response when delivered using a potent adjuvant and an extended vaccination schedule. These data encourage further evaluation of FMP013/ALFQ efficacy and durability in the field.

Imunização intramuscular de camundongos C57BL/6 e BALB/c, com avaliação de títulos de IgG anti-CSP por ELISA, afinidade por ressonância plasmônica de superfície (SPR) e ensaios de inibição de invasão de hepatócitos humanos in vitro (ISI). 42968019.titulo: Association between the december 2020 mass long-lasting insecticidal net distribution campaign and reported malaria incidence in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo: an interrupted time-series analysis of routine surveillance data.
42968019.autores: Mbuku N, Mandja BA, Muntenge G, Nsabatien V, Lukanu P, Wanet S, Mpongo T, Matela B, Zanga J, Gonzalez JP, Luhata C, Matulonga B, Mvuama N

resumo_blocos.racional: A distribuição maciça de mosquiteiros impregnados com inseticidas de ação prolongada constitui o principal pilar para a redução da transmissão de *Plasmodium falciparum* na África Subsaariana, mas sua eficácia populacional sustentada em megacidades hiperendêmicas permanece controversa. Existe uma contradição biológica e epidemiológica não resolvida entre a expansão da cobertura de barreira física/química e o paradoxal aumento de casos clínicos, impulsionado potencialmente por resistência metabólica (upregulation de citocromos P450) e mutações do canal de sódio voltagem-dependente (kdr) em anofelinos, somadas a mudanças no comportamento de picada do vetor. Os autores testaram a hipótese de que a campanha de distribuição de LLINs de dezembro de 2020 em Kinshasa provocou uma inflexão negativa e sustentada na trajetória secular da incidência de malária reportada no período pré e pós-intervenção.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O delineamento baseou-se em uma análise ecológica de séries temporais interrompidas (ITS) utilizando dados mensais de vigilância epidemiológica de malária em Kinshasa, República Democrática do Congo, compreendendo o intervalo longitudinal de janeiro de 2018 a dezembro de 2023. Para a modelagem quantitativa das taxas de incidência sob sobredispersão, ajustaram-se modelos de regressão binomial negativa parametrizados com a população local inserida como offset logarítmico. A estrutura primária segmentada incorporou termos de tempo linear, uma variável binária para a intervenção de dezembro de 2020 e a taxa de variação na inclinação pós-intervenção, com controle rigoroso de sazonalidade via componentes harmônicos de Fourier e marcadores sazonais binários. Como controles analíticos de robustez, foram conduzidas análises de sensibilidade deslocando a janela temporal de intervenção (janeiro e fevereiro de 2021) e aplicando correções de erros-padrão consistentes com heterocedasticidade e autocorrelação (HAC/Newey-West), enquanto a autocorrelação temporal residual foi quantificada pelas funções ACF/PACF e pelo teste formal de Ljung-Box.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A modelagem pré e pós-distribuição revelou, de forma contraintuitiva, uma razão de taxas de incidência (IRR) significativamente maior no período posterior à campanha (IRR = 1,23; IC 95%: 1,07–1,41; p = 0,003), mantendo significância estatística após ajuste por termos sazonais harmônicos de Fourier (IRR = 1,16; IC 95%: 1,03–1,32; p = 0,013). Na análise primária de séries temporais interrompidas segmentada, a introdução dos mosquiteiros correlacionou-se a uma elevação imediata no patamar de incidência (IRR = 1,18; IC 95%: 1,07–1,31; p = 0,001), acompanhada por um aumento modesto, porém estatisticamente significativo, na inclinação mensal subsequente (IRR = 1,01; IC 95%: 1,01–1,02; p < 0,001). As análises de sensibilidade com defasagem temporal (janeiro e fevereiro de 2021) e correção HAC/Newey-West reproduziram com precisão essas estimativas pontuais, embora o teste de Ljung-Box tenha detectado a persistência de autocorrelação residual entre as janelas temporais avaliadas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: A demonstração epidemiológica de que a distribuição em massa de mosquiteiros impregnados com inseticida de longa duração (LLINs) falhou em conter a incidência de malária reforça criticamente a necessidade do LUCHM focar em intervenções biológicas de bloqueio de transmissão que contornem a resistência a piretroides em *Anopheles*. No contexto dos nossos ensaios de biologia celular de *Plasmodium*, os dados evidenciam que a persistência do vetor no campo exige estratégias que visem diretamente as fases sexuais e os estágios esporogônicos do parasita, como o bloqueio da fertilização e a inibição da penetração do oocineto no epitélio intestinal mediada por Pfs25 e Pfs28. Além disso, a manutenção da carga de transmissão ressalta a relevância dos nossos estudos sobre a integridade ultraestrutural da membrana peritrófica do mosquito e as vias de invasão das glândulas salivares por esporozoítos marcados com CSP, oferecendo alvos alternativos não suscetíveis à pressão seletiva inseticida clássica.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Propor ensaios de infecção experimental por membrana (SMFA) comparando a competência vetorial e a suscetibilidade à invasão do intestino médio por *P. falciparum* em colônias de *Anopheles gambiae* resistentes versus sensíveis a piretroides, quantificando a formação de oocistos sob microscopia de fluorescência. Em paralelo, avaliar por microscopia eletrônica de varredura (MEV) a capacidade de anticorpos monoclonais anti-Pfs25 e peptídeos sintéticos anti-CSP em abortar ultraestruturalmente o trânsito do oocineto através da matriz peritrófica de mosquitos previamente expostos a sub-doses de piretroides.

42968019.resumo:
Long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) remain a cornerstone of malaria vector control in sub-Saharan Africa. Although mass LLIN distribution campaigns substantially increase household ownership and access, their population-level effect on malaria incidence may vary over time. We assessed the association between the December 2020 mass LLIN distribution campaign and malaria incidence in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), from 2018 to 2023.
We conducted an ecological interrupted time-series (ITS) study using monthly routine malaria surveillance data from Kinshasa between January 2018 and December 2023. Negative binomial regression models were fitted with population included as a logarithmic offset. The primary segmented ITS model included three explicit ITS terms: calendar time, a binary intervention indicator, and post-intervention time. Seasonality was controlled for using a binary seasonal indicator and Fourier harmonic terms. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using January 2021 and February as alternative intervention start dates and by applying heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation-consistent (HAC/Newey-West) standard errors. Residual temporal autocorrelation was assessed using autocorrelation function (ACF) and partial autocorrelation function (PACF) plots and formal Ljung-Box tests.
In a simple pre/post model, the post-distribution period was associated with higher malaria incidence than the pre-distribution period (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.23, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.07-1.41; p = 0.003). After adjustment for harmonic seasonal terms, this association remained significant (IRR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.03-1.32; p = 0.013). In the primary segmented ITS model, the post-intervention period was associated with a higher incidence level (IRR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.07-1.31; p = 0.001), while post-intervention time was associated with a modest but significant monthly increase in incidence (IRR = 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses using January 2021 and February 2021 as alternative intervention dates, as well as HAC/Newey-West standard errors, yielded highly consistent findings. Significant residual autocorrelation remained present across model specifications.
This ecological ITS analysis did not demonstrate a sustained decline in reported malaria incidence following the December 2020 LLIN distribution campaign in Kinshasa. Findings were robust across alternative intervention dates and autocorrelation-consistent sensitivity analyses but should be interpreted cautiously because of residual autocorrelation, potential reporting changes, the absence of a control group, and the ecological nature of the study.
42968019.metodo: O delineamento baseou-se em uma análise ecológica de séries temporais interrompidas (ITS) utilizando dados mensais de vigilância epidemiológica de malária em Kinshasa, República Democrática do Congo, compreendendo o intervalo longitudinal de janeiro de 2018 a dezembro de 2023. Para a modelagem quantitativa das taxas de incidência sob sobredispersão, ajustaram-se modelos de regressão binomial negativa parametrizados com a população local inserida como offset logarítmico. A estrutura primária segmentada incorporou termos de tempo linear, uma variável binária para a intervenção de dezembro de 2020 e a taxa de variação na inclinação pós-intervenção, com controle rigoroso de sazonalidade via componentes harmônicos de Fourier e marcadores sazonais binários. Como controles analíticos de robustez, foram conduzidas análises de sensibilidade deslocando a janela temporal de intervenção (janeiro e fevereiro de 2021) e aplicando correções de erros-padrão consistentes com heterocedasticidade e autocorrelação (HAC/Newey-West), enquanto a autocorrelação temporal residual foi quantificada pelas funções ACF/PACF e pelo teste formal de Ljung-Box.
42968019.programa: Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão
42968019.implicacao: A demonstração epidemiológica de que a distribuição em massa de mosquiteiros impregnados com inseticida de longa duração (LLINs) falhou em conter a incidência de malária reforça criticamente a necessidade do LUCHM focar em intervenções biológicas de bloqueio de transmissão que contornem a resistência a piretroides em *Anopheles*. No contexto dos nossos ensaios de biologia celular de *Plasmodium*, os dados evidenciam que a persistência do vetor no campo exige estratégias que visem diretamente as fases sexuais e os estágios esporogônicos do parasita, como o bloqueio da fertilização e a inibição da penetração do oocineto no epitélio intestinal mediada por Pfs25 e Pfs28. Além disso, a manutenção da carga de transmissão ressalta a relevância dos nossos estudos sobre a integridade ultraestrutural da membrana peritrófica do mosquito e as vias de invasão das glândulas salivares por esporozoítos marcados com CSP, oferecendo alvos alternativos não suscetíveis à pressão seletiva inseticida clássica.
42968019.faisca_lateral: 💡 Propor ensaios de infecção experimental por membrana (SMFA) comparando a competência vetorial e a suscetibilidade à invasão do intestino médio por *P. falciparum* em colônias de *Anopheles gambiae* resistentes versus sensíveis a piretroides, quantificando a formação de oocistos sob microscopia de fluorescência. Em paralelo, avaliar por microscopia eletrônica de varredura (MEV) a capacidade de anticorpos monoclonais anti-Pfs25 e peptídeos sintéticos anti-CSP em abortar ultraestruturalmente o trânsito do oocineto através da matriz peritrófica de mosquitos previamente expostos a sub-doses de piretroides.

42981406.resumo: Chronic inflammatory vascular diseases are increasingly recognized as systemic disorders sustained by maladaptive cross-organ immunometabolic coupling, yet current therapeutic strategies remain largely lesion-centered and fail to address upstream drivers of disease persistence. Here, we identify the gut-immune-vascular axis as a system-level pathogenic unit that integrates gut microbial dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, metabolic imbalance, and vascular immune activation into a self-reinforcing pathological circuit. Through integrated clinical profiling and cross-species validation, we demonstrate that disruption of this axis is characterized by coordinated probiotic depletion, expansion of proinflammatory taxa, translocation of microbial endotoxins, accumulation of microbiota-derived metabolites, and macrophage polarization toward a proinflammatory phenotype along the gut-vascular continuum. To therapeutically target this axis, we engineer enzyme-responsive synbiotic microspheres that codeliver probiotics, a microbial metabolic pathway inhibitor, and a prebiotic within a protective polymeric matrix, enabling site-specific intestinal activation and coordinated microbiota-metabolic modulation. This engineered system restores intestinal barrier integrity, reprograms microbial ecology and metabolite output, suppresses immunometabolic dysfunction, and robustly attenuates pathological vascular remodeling across cellular, murine, and large-animal models, with in-stent restenosis serving as a representative disease context. Collectively, this work establishes axis-oriented immunometabolic reprogramming as a generalizable therapeutic paradigm and highlights engineered synbiotic platforms as scalable tools for system-level intervention in chronic inflammatory diseases.

42981187.resumo: Epidemiological evidence linking asthma to lung cancer risk remains contradictory, presenting asthma as either a risk factor or a protective condition. We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

42979823.resumo:
Lupus nephritis (LN) is a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and current therapies often fail to prevent end-stage renal disease. Follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL1), a mesenchymal/stromal-derived glycoprotein, is implicated in renal inflammation.
To synthesize evidence for a proposed FSTL1-driven NLRP3 inflammasome axis in LN and to identify gaps relevant to biomarker development and targeted therapy.
We examine the hypothesis that stromal/tubular FSTL1 is internalized by macrophages and activates NLRP3 via dual signals: mitochondrial ATP production (activation) and transcriptional upregulation of Nlrp3/pro-caspase-1 (priming), with resulting IL-1β amplifying tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis. We assess evidence that FSTL1 is elevated in SLE sera, whereas direct LN kidney evidence is limited to one Chinese-language immunohistochemical study and NLRP3 colocalization has not been demonstrated in biopsy-proven LN; CKD and UUO models suggest FSTL1 may be present in LN kidney but this remains untested. We also discuss post-translational modifications, extracellular vesicle shuttling, and immunometabolism as unexplored determinants of context-dependent FSTL1 behavior.
The proposed mesenchyme/stroma-to-macrophage axis may offer new opportunities for LN biomarkers and targeted therapy, but current evidence is largely indirect and should be interpreted as a mechanistic framework requiring rigorous translational validation.

42977746.resumo: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α-XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α-XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte-IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

42977568.resumo: Sepsis-related cytokine storm is associated with poor prognosis in septic patients. IFNγ/LPS can synergistically trigger a sepsis-associated proinflammatory cytokine storm and induce macrophage death in the form of PANoptosis. The ensuing release of proinflammatory cytokines further amplifies macrophage death, leading to subsequent multiple organ damage. Concurrently, the IFNγ/LPS induced inflammatory cascade also downregulates chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) activity, and this dysregulation further exacerbates the inflammatory response in macrophages and in vivo. Thus, a positive feedback loop between dysfunctional CMA and the inflammatory cascade is established. Enhancing CMA activation reduces macrophage death and organ damage, whereas inhibiting CMA exacerbates macrophage PANoptosis and organ injury. Mechanistically, impaired CMA leads to accumulation of the transcription factor CUX1, which subsequently upregulates Pyrin expression and promotes Pyrin-mediated PANoptosome assembly, thereby driving macrophage PANoptosis. In addition to the cytokine storm, the lacylation at lysine 561 (K561) of HSC70, a core component of the CMA machinery, is associated with reduced CMA activity. Blocking lactylation can similarly attenuate macrophage death and multiple organ injury in sepsis. Taken together, this "Kla-CMA-CUX1/Pyrin-PANoptosis" signaling axis, linking metabolic reprogramming to immune dysregulation in sepsis, suggests that targeting key nodes of this axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy to reduce sepsis-associated mortality.

42977100.resumo: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an exceptionally aggressive, therapy-resistant central nervous system malignancy. Within the tumour microenvironment, glioblastoma-associated microglia and macrophages (GAMs) constitute a highly heterogeneous population whose functional states profoundly influence disease progression, tissue architecture, immune evasion, and treatment response. In this review, we propose a conceptual framework in which distinct GAM phenotypes emerge from the integrated influence of vascular, tumoural, metabolic, biomechanical, neural, and immune inputs, together with glyco-immune interactions, extracellular vesicles, and epigenetic regulation. As GAMs process these cues, they actively remodel their surrounding ecosystem, sustaining a protumourigenic niche. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic interventions-including those targeting GAM abundance, immunometabolism, mechanotransduction, and intercellular communication-as well as advanced platforms such as engineered myeloid systems, phytomedicines, targeted delivery vehicles, and gut-brain axis-based strategies. Furthermore, we address key translational bottlenecks, including extreme GAM plasticity, spatial heterogeneity, limitations of preclinical models, barriers to central nervous system delivery, and a lack of predictive biomarkers. We argue that the therapeutically relevant target is not the GAM population in isolation, but rather the diverse niche-GAM functional units and the cumulative signalling networks that sustain them. Ultimately, achieving durable clinical efficacy will require biomarker-guided, spatially informed combination regimens that selectively disrupt maladaptive myeloid states while preserving physiological microglial homeostasis.

42977003.resumo:
Huangqin Tang (HQT), documented in the Shanghan Lun, is traditionally prescribed for "dysenteric disorders" (Li Ji). Modern clinical studies confirm its efficacy against ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer-associated inflammation, providing a verified traditional basis for investigating its immunomodulatory effects in colorectal malignancy. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of lactate-induced protein lactylation in MIF-driven PD-1 resistance and to determine if HQT can reverse this phenotype through metabolic reprogramming.
CT26-bearing BALB/c mice were administered HQT intragastrically combined with intraperitoneal anti-PD-1 antibodies. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were profiled by flow cytometry. Integrative transcriptomics and network pharmacology were utilized to screen candidate targets. LC-MS/MS-based lactylomic profiling identified specific modification sites. Lactate modulation assays, and site-directed mutagenesis (NF-κB1 K249R) coupled with rescue experiments were performed in vitro to validate the molecular cascade mechanistically.
HQT synergized with anti-PD-1 to suppress tumor growth and prolong survival. This combination remodeled the immune microenvironment, increasing CD8+ T cells and M1-like macrophages while reducing M2 macrophages and MDSCs. Mechanistically, HQT inhibited tumor glycolysis and lactate production. Lactylomic analysis revealed that lactate induced NF-κB1 lysine 249 (K249) lactylation in CD4+ Tregs, driving MIF transcription. Introducing the K249R mutation abolished lactate-induced MIF expression and reversed immunosuppression. HQT effectively reduced NF-κB1 K249 lactylation, disrupting the MIF-driven feedback loop.
NF-κB1 K249 lactylation acts as a critical post-translational switch linking tumor glycolysis to Treg-mediated immunosuppression. HQT overcomes PD-1 resistance by suppressing this axis. These findings support combining metabolic intervention with immunotherapy and highlight K249 lactylation as a potential biomarker for treatment response.
